name: ktema-capi-0.1.0
readme:
# Ktema C surface, 0.1.0

The engine that keeps state on a device that has no operating system, as a static library
and a header. The source of the engine is not in this package; what is here is the
contract, an implementation of it for each target named below, and the specification the
implementation writes.

Read `RELEASE` for what this build is and what it was built from. Read
`targets/<target>/LINKING` before you link: it states what the library provides, the two
hooks you supply, and what moves the ABI number.

## Five minutes

On a machine with a C compiler and an operating system, the package for your host runs:

```sh
cd targets/aarch64-apple-darwin
cc -I include example.c lib/libktema_capi.a -o example && ./example
echo $?     # 0 is four records written and walked
```

On a device, replace the medium in `example.c` with your own read, write, list, and delete,
supply `ktma_enter_critical` and `ktma_exit_critical`, and link the object for your target.
The header states what the engine expects of that medium; `example.c` is one written out.

## What is in here

    RELEASE                  version, abi, format, revision, targets, digests
    CHANGELOG.md             what each ABI number means, and when it moved
    spec/                    the format the artifact writes, and the medium contract
    targets/<target>/        include/ktema.h, lib/libktema_capi.a, example.c, VERSION, LINKING
    targets/<target>.tar.gz  the same directory, archived
    SHA256SUMS               every file above

## Targets in this release

Built:

    riscv32imac-unknown-none-elf
    thumbv7em-none-eabihf
    aarch64-apple-darwin

Not built on the host that assembled this release, and not claimed by it:

    xtensa-esp32s3-none-elf
changelog:
# The C surface's ABI

`KTMA_ABI_VERSION` numbers the C surface: the signatures, the constants, and the contract
in `include/ktema.h`. It is not the format version. The format version says what a volume
holds and moves independently; this says what a caller must have compiled against.

The number moves when a change would break a caller compiled against the previous header:
a removed entry point, a renamed one, a changed signature, a changed constant that a caller
branches on, or a changed obligation on the caller. An entry point added to a later build
keeps the number, so a build that adds one stays compatible with every caller that does not
use it.

A release states its number in `RELEASE`, in each `targets/<target>/VERSION`, and in the
artifact's file name. `ktma_abi_version()` reports it at run time and `KTMA_ABI_VERSION`
states it at compile time, so one comparison at startup catches a header and a library from
different builds.

`crates/capi/release.sh` refuses to assemble a release whose ABI has no row below. A new
number cannot ship before someone has written what it means.

| ABI | Set on | What it means |
|---|---|---|
| 7 | 2026-11-18 | The first number a distributed artifact carries. The surface is `ktma_*` throughout, the header declares 32 entry points, and the two integrator hooks are `ktma_enter_critical` and `ktma_exit_critical`. |
| 6 | 2026-10-03 | Set while the surface was `ktema_*`. The prefix moved to `ktma_*` on 2026-10-26 and the number did not move with it, so a caller compiled against six before that date cannot link a library built after it: every symbol it names is gone. No artifact of that era was distributed. Seven exists so that a number handed to an outside team means one thing. |
